localizedValues.name: Backcountry Registration
localizedValues.description: Permit Registration allows for overnight camping year-round in most areas within E.C. Manning Park. Backcountry Reservations are required at Buckhorn, Kicking Horse and Frosty Creek campgrounds in peak season.

localizedValues.name: Buckhorn
localizedValues.description: Reservations are required from the Canada Day weekend to Labour Day. Permit registration is required outside of this time period. Buckhorn backcountry campground was re-constructed in 2021 and is located along the Heather Trail approximately 4.5 km from the Blackwall parking lot. Campground amenities include 24 raised wooden tent platforms, food caches and pit toilets – fires are not permitted. Water can be gathered from the small creek that cuts through the campground but please treat the water before use. There is also a cooking/emergency shelter available for all Heather trail hikers.

localizedValues.name: Kicking Horse
localizedValues.description: Reservations are required from the Canada Day weekend to Labour Day. Permit registration is required outside of this time period. A little over 8km north of Buckhorn campground on the Heather Trail is Kicking Horse Campground, a great option for those willing to hike a little further from their start at Blackwall Mountain or as a subsequent destination for those linking backcountry campgrounds on a multi-day trip.  From Buckhorn campground, the Heather Trail gains elevation and then meanders through sub-alpine meadows before descending to Kicking Horse campground. Kicking Horse campground is a great overnight option at the end of a good day hike before heading back, or as a first stop before heading to Nicomen Lake, Grainger Creek or beyond. The campground is moderately treed and provides some protection from wind and rain. Sites may have decked, framed earth, or dirt pads. Food storage lockers and pit toilets are available.

localizedValues.name: Frosty Creek
localizedValues.description: Reservations are required during peak season. Permit registration is required outside of this time period. Frosty Creek campground offers the best option for those wanting to explore Mt. Frosty for consecutive days. It offers a shaded and protected staging area prior to day hiking to the meadows or Mt. Frosty’s summit and can also be a good first or last night’s camp when linking the Similkameen and Windy Joe Trails and the P.C.T. camp. To protect the fragile sub-alpine environment, camping is not permitted anywhere other than the campground’s designated sites. The campground is moderately treed and provides some protection from wind and rain. Sites may have decked, framed earth, or dirt pads. Food storage lockers and pit toilets are available. A small shelter is available but is for emergency use only.

localizedValues.name: G1 - Lone Duck 1
localizedValues.description: Lone Duck 1 & 2 each consist of a shelter complete with picnic tables and wood stove (no firewood), pit toilets, flush toilets, large outside dish sinks, grassy area for tents, a parking lot and the use of showers at Lightning Lake campground. (summer only) Both group sites overlook Lone Duck Bay on Lightning Lake. Water is not guaranteed at the campground, due to fluctuating snow levels throughout the year. Be prepared to bring your own water and use pit toilets during your stay. Lone Duck 1 is the First Come First Serve Winter Campground after Thanksgiving weekend.
